title: Coding is no longer the bottleneck.
required: Coding is no longer the bottleneck.
AI writes code in minutes, but without a delivery system it inflates PRs, shifts the bottleneck to review, and degrades delivery stability.
A system no one can safely change.

title: Build the right thing. Build it to last.
required: Build the right thing. Build it to last.
Product strategy decides what is worth building.
our focus is delivering it as software that lasts.
Frame the problem · weigh trade-offs · test with prototypes
Prototypes test assumptions. A delivery system ships production software.

title: Three boundaries around AI code.
required: Agents work inside the system. Engineers remain in charge of it.
How code is written, checked, and shipped.
What running code is permitted to touch

title: Standardising delivery.
required: One governed path from change to production
across how code is written and how it ships.

title: Constrain code authoring.
required: Isolate the workspace, share one set of engineering standards, and enforce architectural rules at compile time.
Architectural and safety rules enforced at compile time.
Reviewers focus on design and trade-offs—not policing mechanical rules.

title: Automate verification and deployment.
required: Agent-written unit tests often repeat the agent's own bugs—pipelines must replay behaviour against the spec, gate the supply chain, and automate deployment.
One immutable artifact deployed with its verification evidence.

title: Specifying behaviour.
required: People and agents share one source of truth: durable specifications, not code.

title: Prompts are not specifications.
required: Prompts disappear after a turn and leave agents to guess. Specifications persist in the repo as the contract both people and agents build against.

title: The agentic development loop.
required: Align on intent upfront, break work into bounded slices for agents, and verify code against the spec.
Units of work, ordered by dependency
Every change runs the loop. Any spec change re-enters the human review gate.

title: Code is disposable. Specifications are durable.
required: Code is generated from the spec. The sealed specification is what you keep.
Regenerate the plan. Rebuild the code. The specification remains.

title: Sandboxing execution.
required: Grant generated code nothing by default
it reaches infrastructure only through host-mediated capabilities.

title: Zero trust for generated code.
required: Containers give every dependency ambient access to network, files, and secrets. WASI components start with zero authority and use only the capabilities the host links.

title: Business logic in the guest. Plumbing in the host.
required: Because the runtime bridges infrastructure and external resources, agents generate pure business logic—not plumbing.
Domain rules, state transitions, and typed capability calls.
Bridges external services, clients, credentials, and connection pools.
Less code for agents to generate. Far fewer ways to get it wrong.

title: Infrastructure portability.
required: Write code once against capability contracts. Bind them to local, cloud, or on-premise services at deploy time.

title: Use cases.
required: Prototype, legacy codebase, or new service—every change runs the same governed path.

title: Run smaller, local models.
required: Frontier models are needed to invent architecture—not to fill in pre-scaffolded, compiler-checked slices.
Invent structure · choose libraries · hold the full codebase in context
Structure and tests pre-built · fill bounded logic · verify at compile time
Today: frontier models in production · Next: open-weight and client-hosted models.

title: Close the loop on issues.
required: Detect an issue, analyse and propose a fix, approve the spec change, and build and deploy across code and infrastructure.

title: Thank you.
required: 25 years of critical-software judgement, now applied to accountable delivery at AI speed.
